name: Saints Pontian and Hippolytus
history: Pontian was Bishop of Rome and Hippolytus a learned Roman priest who had set himself up as a rival bishop. In 235 the Emperor Maximinus sent them both to the mines of Sardinia, where they died. Tradition holds that they were reconciled there, and both are honoured as martyrs.
life: Hippolytus was the most important theologian of the Roman Church in the early third century, writing in Greek on Scripture and against the heresies of his time. He thought Pope Callistus too lenient towards repentant sinners and too unclear in his teaching, broke with him and was chosen bishop by a group of followers, the first antipope we know of. The schism lasted into the time of Pope Pontian. When Maximinus Thrax turned on the Church’s leaders in 235, he exiled both men to the mines of Sardinia, where few survived. Pontian resigned his office so that Rome could elect a successor, the first pope known to have done so. Hippolytus is believed to have returned to unity with the Church and urged his followers to do the same. Both died in exile, and Pope Fabian brought their bodies back to Rome to be buried with honour.
prayerTo: Saints Pontian and Hippolytus, you were divided in life and united in suffering for Christ. Pray for all who are estranged within the Church and among Christians, that we may be reconciled before it is too late. Help me to put the unity of the Church above my own opinions. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the unity of Christians, and make peace with someone in your parish or family with whom you have quarrelled.
meditation: A rival bishop and a pope died side by side in the mines. Is there a disagreement you are holding on to that you could lay down for the sake of peace?
